packages.label: יָדַיִן וְרַגְלַיִן
packages.reason: All these nodes share the essential nature of ידים/רגלים — the revelation of divine light through the body's extremities. The teaching equates: the explicit Torah (nigleh) = hands; the esoteric Torah (nistar) = feet; Mordechai = hands (dror/freedom = engraving on tablets); Esther = feet (shokayin/hidden); clapping (hamchat kaf) = hands; dancing (rikudin) = feet; kimu = feet; kiblu = hands; the omer = Mordechai; the barley = Esther; the Shechina = isha = Esther; KBH = ish = Mordechai. All these are bechina-equivalent expressions of the same limb-structure of holiness.
merge_notes: Merged in 2-node isolated component {"רגלי עמדה במישור", אמונה}: 'רגלי עמדה במישור' is the positive state of the feet (Tehilim 26:12), equated with emunah — the direct output of the hands/feet system being rectified. Shared nature: emunah = the stable feet = the rectified foot-dimension of holiness.

packages.label: צַדִּיק וְרוּחַ
packages.reason: All these nodes share the essential nature of the tzaddik as the spiritual wind/spirit that animates and rectifies. The teaching equates: tzaddik = ruach (Bamidbar 27); ruach shbalev = the tzaddik; Yosef = the tzaddik (the one through whom hands and feet are raised); 'dofeik' (knocking) = ruach (Tikkunim 25:68); mishpatim = ruach (Yeshayahu 28:6); Yaakov = sekhel/wisdom (Onkelos on Bereshit 27); the tzaddik = son of wisdom (av = wisdom). Tikkun hame'uvat = Yosef's domain. Shimon (the rebuker) and 'ki shama H' ki senuah anochi' share the nature of the one who hears and rebukes — the tzaddik's corrective function.
merge_notes: Raw bechina component: {צדיק, רוח, רוח שבלב, יוסף, דופק, משפטים, תקון המעות} — 7 nodes.

Merged {יעקב, חכמה}: Yaakov = sekhel is the tzaddik's cognitive dimension; the text explicitly states 'Yaakov hu bechina hasechel' (section ד). Nature: wisdom/sekhel = tzaddik's inner identity = the rebuking authority.
Merged {שמעון, כי שמע ה}: Shimon represents the tzaddik's rebuke capacity — 'the one who rebukes is hated' (Ketubot 105b). Shared nature: corrective/rebuking function of tzaddik-wisdom.

packages.label: גַּאֲוָה וַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
packages.reason: All these nodes share the essential nature of the evil side — pride as idolatry, and its associated manifestations. The teaching equates: המן = avodah zarah (the Sages say he made himself an idol); גאוה = avodah zarah (Mishlei 16: tovat H kol gevah lev); תוספות/ribui = gaavah (Devarim 7: lo meruvchem; also 've'eleh mosif al harishonim' = Haman-Amalek); גאות = המן's defining quality. The minim (heretics) and 'natavu raglai' share the evil nature — heresy = the fallen/deflected feet. Sitra demota = akum = the evil dimension opposed to God's glorification. The body/sack (guf) without correction is the vessel of persistent desires — not inherently evil but in this Torah appears in the context of ba'alei gaavah whose fasting fails.
merge_notes: Raw bechina component: {גאוה, עבודה זרה, המן, גאות, תוספות} — 5 nodes.

Merged {מינות, נטיו רגלי}: מינות (heresy/atheism) is the evil counterpart to אמונה; 'natavu raglai' is the fallen feet — the evil version of the feet dimension. Shared nature: the deflected/corrupted foot-dimension of evil = minut.

Merged {סטרא דמותא, עכו"ם}: Both express the domain of death/evil from which idolatry emanates; akum = sitra demota in this Torah. Shared nature: the realm of spiritual death that opposes divine revelation.

Merged {שק, גוף}: The body-as-sack metaphor appears in the context of ba'alei gaavah — their fasting empties the sack but leaves the holes (desires). The nature is: body = vessel of uncorrected desires = the physical substrate of gaavah.

packages.label: תְּפִלָּה וּבַיִת
packages.reason: Both pairs share the nature of prayer as the elevated, accessible form of divine service — the 'bayit' level where even non-Jews can grasp God's greatness. 'Eishet' = roshei teivot 'Adonai Sefatai Tiftach' = tefila. 'Bayit' = ir Elokeinu = the place of prayer accessible to all peoples (Yeshayahu 56:7). These two pairs are thematically identical: the essence of prayer as the bayit-house, the settled/inhabited place of the divine. They form the stated goal of the Torah's first sections (gimel-dalet).
merge_notes: Two isolated 2-node components merged: {אשת, תפלה} + {בית, עיר אלקינו}.

Justification: Both express the nature of prayer as the 'bayit' form — the accessible, inhabited manifestation of divine service. 'Eishet' = tefila (roshei teivot Adonai Sefatai Tiftach). 'Bayit' = ir Elokeinu = the place of tefila for all peoples. The Torah explicitly links these: 'ki veiti beit tefila yikarei lekhol ha'amim' (Yeshayahu 56:7). Shared nature: tefila at the bayit/ir level.
